title: Sandboxed Quant Heuristics & Onboarding Capture — Apr 29 2028
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick capture from this week’s sandboxed experiments and the onboarding sync with Solutions Eng. Focus: cheap-ish 4-bit variants + KV-cache interaction and a tiny eval sweep for hallucination/regression checks on the onboarding model (codenamed ‘opal-7b-compact’). This is intentionally a rough working log — notes to self + action items for next sprint.

Meeting snapshot (2028-04-29, 10:00 PT) — attendees: Priya, Evan, Mariana, Jonah, Sasha (SE):
- 10m: goals recap — ship baseline quant profile that meets latency SLO for Dedicated tier and passes smoke evals.
- 20m: experiment readouts from sandbox (see results below).
- 15m: onboarding checklist for opal-7b-compact; solved tokenization mismatch reported by SEs.
- 10m: next steps + owners.

What we ran this week (sandbox cluster):
- Variant A: opal-7b-compact fp16 baseline (baseline for perf/quality).
- Variant B: opal-7b-compact 4-bit per-tensor asymmetric (PTA) with outlier handling for FFN layers.
- Variant C: 4-bit + selective 8-bit for KV projection matrices (heuristic: top-2 attention heads kept at 8-bit).
- Microbatch config sweep: microbatch sizes [1,2,4]; continuous batching turned on for sizes >1.
- KV cache policy tests: full-KV persist vs ephemeral per-request (simulate short chat vs stateless gen).

Quick quantitative readouts (median of 50 runs, p95 where called):
- Latency (tokens/sec normalized to baseline fp16 = 1.0):
  - Variant A (fp16): 1.00 median, p95 1.12
  - Variant B (4-bit PTA): 1.42 median, p95 1.58 (good speedup but outlier tokens occasionally spike latency)
  - Variant C (4-bit selective KV 8b): 1.28 median, p95 1.35 (smoother tail than B)
- Memory footprint (approx GPU VRAM used / model):
  - A: 22GB
  - B: 12.2GB
  - C: 14.1GB
- Cost proxy (tokens/sec * effective batch factor): Variant B shows ~35% cost reduction vs A; C ~25%.

Quality/eval snapshot (small eval harness: 240 examples, mix of QA/opinion/MCQ):
- Perplexity delta vs fp16 baseline (lower better):
  - B: +0.9% (acceptable for many tasks)
  - C: +0.4%
- Hallucination spot-check (30 open-ended QA prompts):
  - A: 2 hallucinations (baseline)
  - B: 5 hallucinations (notable increase on numeric references)
  - C: 3 hallucinations
- Specific failure mode observed: B degrades on arithmetic-like numeric references and long-context citations — seems correlated with extreme weights in a small subset of FFN neurons (we traced to two outlier ranges).

Operational observations (informal):
- KV-cache + 4-bit interaction: pure 4-bit (B) + full-KV persist shows occasional correctness regressions under long-context streaming (seen in the chat-like sequences). We suspect the quantization noise compounds in KV projections when the cache is long (>1024 tokens).
- Selective 8-bit for KV projection (C) stabilizes both quality and tail latency; gives better p95 due to fewer decode retries and fewer fallback triggers in our runtime.
- Continuous batching helps amortize decode overhead for microbatch >1, but increases p95 for small requests if autoscaler isn’t tuned to maintain concurrency.
- Prefetch + prefix caching: prefix cache hits reduce token computation by ~12% in our chat sim; TTL policy needs to be tuned to avoid stale facts during evals.

Decisions from sync:
- Default quant profile for onboarding opal-7b-compact will use variant C (4-bit with selective 8-bit for KV projections) for Dedicated tier rollout candidate. Rationale: smoother tail and fewer hallucination regressions.
- Create a guardrail in serving runtime: if cache length > 2048 tokens and model is running in 4-bit full mode, route to selective-8b variant or fallback to model-split instance.
- Add a simple eval gating check: any quant variant must not increase hallucination rate by >2x baseline on the small hallucination suite; otherwise mark for rollback.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Priya: push a reproducible minimal test that demonstrates the FFN outlier effect in a colab-style notebook; include weight histograms and per-layer quant error plots. ETA: 2028-05-04.
- Evan: add runtime flag for automatic KV-projection upcast when cache length exceeds threshold; write unit+integration tests. ETA: 2028-05-08.
- Mariana: expand eval suite to 1k prompts with structured categories (numeric, citation, instruction-chaining); integrate into CI smoke target. ETA: 2028-05-11.
- Jonah: coordinate with Solutions Eng to stage Dedicated onboarding job with variant C and report telemetry (latency, token-cost, rollback triggers). ETA: 2028-05-06.
- All: short postmortem if rollback occurs during staged onboard (owners TBD by incident).

Open questions / TODOs (brainstorm fragments):
- Is there a lightweight heuristic to detect when per-token quant noise will compound (e.g., KL divergence on softmax logits across first 32 tokens)?
- Should we instrument per-head quant error during online serving and emit a telemetry signal instead of static thresholds? Cost/PCI egress concerns for telemetry.
- Explore a hybrid scheme: dynamic per-request upcast based on context length and request type (chat vs completion). Complexity vs benefit trade-off?

Notes to self (in-the-weeds):
- The two FFN outlier ranges are predominantly in layer 10 & 14 (0-indexed) in the current opal topology; investigate whether masked LM pretraining skewed those distributions.
- Try compressing bias-only parameters at 2-bit as a microprobe — low ROI but cheap to test.
- Remember to update the model-catalog entry with quant profile metadata + perf numbers once we stabilize.

Quick linkages / references:
- Sandbox experiment notebook: https://internal-sandbox/redwood/opal-quant/exp-187
- Jira: RDW-1124 (opal-7b-compact onboarding), RDW-1186 (runtime kv-upcast)
- PR with kernel changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/893

Retro / what worked well:
- Running micro-sweeps in isolated sandbox with fixed random seeds gave highly reproducible medians; allowed us to triage the outlier case faster.
- Quick SE feedback loop (Sasha) helped prioritize the selective-8b trade-off quickly; kept the deck small for the Dedicated pilot.

Bottom line (one-liner):
- Variant C (4-bit with selective 8-bit on KV) is our best candidate for opal-7b-compact onboarding to Dedicated — fastest credible win in cost without unacceptable quality regressions; operational guardrails required for very long contexts.

---
Next check-in: 2028-05-06 (standup + telemetry readout).

Unresolved: schedule a deeper noise-analysis session (2h) to attempt an algorithmic mitigation for the FFN outliers; action: Priya to propose agenda by 2028-05-02.

End of capture.
